nodes.label: Patient had discrete, dark red, circular lesions in his right axilla for 3 months
The patient is a man in his 40s with severe pruritus at the lesion sites that wakes him at night.

He denied recent trauma, history of similar lesions, associated pain, blisters, or systemic symptoms (fever, chills); medical history was unremarkable, with no environmental triggers or new medications.
Treatment with over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream, ketoconazole cream, and discontinuation of underarm deodorant yielded no improvement.

Physical examination revealed 3 well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches without scale or erosion limited to the right axilla; no other skin or mucous membrane lesions were noted, and Wood lamp examination was negative.
